components.html: Frame Academy

narrative.overview:
The next frame identifies a course or a useful next step. Bright reading surfaces, precise blue actions and two offset open corners give practical creative learning a clear, active identity. Authored examples lead the discovery experience; the learning interface gives the lesson, practice note and next action more room than decoration.

This is the implemented Frame system, extracted on 14 October 2026 from the responsive website, Flutter app, editable identity masters and workbook stylesheet. The approved language comes from [direction-contract.md](direction-contract.md) and [identity-spec.md](identity-spec.md). Frame Academy is the full brand; Frame is its compact app name. The identity remains scoped to this project. The agency root `DESIGN.md` and `.impeccable/design.json` continue to own the CR8.Media shell.

Final native source recheck records explicit zero Arabic tracking, photograph/title separation, UIScene course delivery and guarded refreshes. The native verification record names actual English/Arabic simulator journeys and separates widget accessibility checks from physical-device certification.
keyCharacteristics: Bright canvas, dark reading text, blue actions and limited mint/coral teaching artwork.
A custom vector wordmark and two offset L corners with a fixed orientation.
Different density for discovery, learning and workbook reading, with a shared hierarchy.
Textual progress and a named next lesson beside the primary action.
Natural Arabic shaping, readable Latin records and equivalent recovery actions.

rules.name: The Confirmed State Rule
rules.body: A saved color or completion icon accompanies a confirmed operation and written status. Color alone never asserts saved progress.

rules.name: The Arabic Shaping Rule
rules.body: Arabic uses its local family and natural spacing. Keep identity geometry fixed, isolate Latin records, and let translated labels wrap rather than shrinking them to match English.

rules.name: The Immediate Reduction Rule
rules.body: Device reduced motion removes the website's transitions, animations, smooth scrolling and artwork lift. Native route motion follows Flutter's platform transition behavior and device accessibility preference; verification claims must point to the native record.

rules.name: The Fixed Mark Rule
rules.body: Preserve the two offset L paths and their orientation. Mirror directional interface cues independently; do not borrow Form's single architectural frame or close the Frame window.

dos: Do retain Studio White, Midnight Ink, Frame Blue and the approved limited Mint/Coral roles.
Do keep the custom identity masters, two offset L paths, butt endpoints and fixed orientation.
Do place course decision facts before commitment and the named next lesson beside textual progress.
Do use actual course artwork, media and implementation captures with their recorded provenance.
Do preserve entered work through failure and wait for acknowledged persistence before saved feedback.
Do shape Arabic naturally, isolate Latin records and allow text expansion and device scaling.
Do keep the Frame world scoped separately from the CR8.Media shell and Form Architecture.
donts: Don't use small White functional text on Mint or Coral, or Blueprint Rule as a necessary field boundary.
Don't mirror the identity mark or the authored photographic comparison with the interface.
Don't complete a lesson when it is opened or played, or describe a saved draft as completion.
Don't autoplay media or make hover the only way to reveal a course or action.
Don't turn planned curriculum durations into produced-video claims.
Don't add instructors, reviews, credentials, learner counts, client history or business outcomes without evidence.
